title: Étale inverse image: ring lift and hom-set comparison
statement: Let U and V be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and f : U → V any morphism. On their small étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], let L = Scheme.etaleSetPullback f be the set inverse image [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and assume L preserves finite limits. Let Rr be direct image on commutative-ring-valued sheaves, defined by precomposition with base change, and FrU, FrV the forgetful functors to set sheaves. There exist Lr, an adjunction ar : Lr ⊣ Rr, and a natural isomorphism er : Lr ⋙ FrU ≅ FrV ⋙ L. For all G, F and h : Lr G → F, FrV(ar.homEquiv G F h) = a.homEquiv (FrV G) (FrU F) (er_G⁻¹ ≫ FrU(h)), where a is the set adjunction. For every G there are source and target sheaf morphisms representing sectionwise addition, zero, negation, multiplication and one. Each binary operation op satisfies L(opV) = prodComparison L ≫ prod.map er_G⁻¹ er_G⁻¹ ≫ opU ≫ er_G; each constant c satisfies L(cV) = terminal.from _ ≫ cU ≫ er_G; negation satisfies L(negV) = er_G⁻¹ ≫ negU ≫ er_G. All section formulas use the chosen product projections and chosen terminal sheaves. No unit compatibility or abelian inverse-image comparison is assumed in this lemma.

proof.text: The base-change functor is continuous. The recorded set inverse image is left adjoint to its sectionwise set direct image by Mathlib.sheafAdjunctionContinuous. The assumed finite-limit preservation implies finite-product preservation.

Use the ring clause of the sheaf/internal-object identification on the source and target sites; its section formulas identify the structure maps with the actual sectionwise operations. Apply the corresponding clause of the product-preserving lifted adjunction to the set adjunction.

Transport the lifted adjunction through the inverse sheaf/internal-object functors. Its right lift evaluates at base-changed objects and hence has exactly the sectionwise operations and restriction maps of the recorded direct image. The resulting right forgetful comparison is the identity; restrict the hom-set equations of the generic lift accordingly.

Take the sectionwise operations supplied by the sheaf/internal-object identification. Naturality of the product comparison gives the binary-operation equations after composing with its inverse and cancelling the isomorphism. For constants use uniqueness of the map to the terminal sheaf, and for negation use the inverse comparison component. The section formulas are the source and target identification formulas.
